title: The Promise of a Ranking
fact_notes: オリジナル論説・架空事例。実在の天体・実証結果・人物・法令ではない。台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A ranking can provide a convenient way of organizing information about a collection of people, organizations or activities according to a selected characteristic.
sentences.ja: 順位は選ばれた特性に従って人々、組織、活動の集合についての情報を整理する便利な方法を提供できる。

sentences.en: The simplicity of the resulting order may nevertheless encourage readers to attach significance to differences between positions without examining the process by which those positions were determined.
sentences.ja: それでも結果の順序の単純さは、その順位が決まった過程を調べずに順位差に意味を付与するよう読者を促すことがある。

sentences.en: This possibility becomes ethically significant when a ranking influences the opportunities available to the people or organizations that it describes.
sentences.ja: 順位が記述対象の人や組織に利用可能な機会に影響するとき、この可能性は倫理的に重要になる。

sentences.en: A fictional competition involving school projects illustrates the relationship between the purpose of an evaluation and the way its results are communicated.
sentences.ja: 学校活動の架空競技は評価の目的と結果の伝達方法の関係を例示する。

sentences.en: Imagine that several student groups submit proposals for activities intended to benefit their local community, and that the organizers have enough resources to support only a limited number of the proposals.
sentences.ja: 複数班が地域に利益をもたらす活動案を出し、主催者は限られた数の提案を支援する資源しかないと想像しよう。

sentences.en: The organizers evaluate each proposal by examining its potential contribution to the community, its practical feasibility, and the way the students have explained their plans.
sentences.ja: 主催者は地域への潜在的貢献、実務上の実現可能性、生徒による計画説明方法を調べ各提案を評価する。

sentences.en: They then combine the assessments into a numerical score and use the resulting scores to help select the proposals that will receive support.
sentences.ja: 次に評価を数値点にまとめ、その得点を支援対象提案の選択に用いる。

sentences.en: One organizer suggests publishing a complete ranking of the groups so that everybody can see the outcome of the competition.
sentences.ja: ある主催者は全員が競技の結果を見られるよう班の完全な順位を公開する提案をする。

sentences.en: Another questions whether the ranking would adequately communicate the information that groups need in order to improve their proposals.
sentences.ja: 別の者は順位が班の提案改善に必要な情報を十分伝えるか疑問視する。

sentences.en: Two proposals with similar overall scores may have quite different strengths and limitations.
sentences.ja: 同程度の総合得点の二提案もかなり異なる強みや限界を持ち得る。

sentences.en: One group might have identified a valuable objective but failed to explain how it would obtain the resources necessary to achieve it, while another might have produced a feasible plan whose intended contribution to the community remained uncertain.
sentences.ja: 一班は価値ある目的を特定しても達成に必要な資源の取得方法を説明できず、別班は実現可能だが地域への想定貢献が不確かな計画を作ったかもしれない。

sentences.en: The ranking might indicate which proposal received the higher combined score without distinguishing the different kinds of improvement that each proposal would require.
sentences.ja: 順位はどちらが高い総合点を得たか示しても、各提案に必要な異なる改善種類を区別しないかもしれない。

sentences.en: Furthermore, a small difference in scores might not establish that one proposal is superior to another in every respect.
sentences.ja: さらに小さな得点差は一提案が他よりあらゆる点で優れていることを確定しないかもしれない。

sentences.en: The organizers consequently recognize that a procedure designed to support a selection decision does not necessarily produce a complete account of the qualities of every participant.
sentences.ja: そこで選択判断を支援するため設計された手順が、必ずしも全参加者の質の完全な説明を生まないと主催者は認識する。

sentences.en: The fictional organizers consider providing feedback that describes the relationship between the stated criteria and the particular features of each proposal.
sentences.ja: 架空主催者は明示基準と各提案の特定特徴の関係を記述するフィードバックの提供を考える。

sentences.en: They also discuss how much information about individual scores should be communicated publicly, taking into account the purpose of the announcement and the expectations of the students who submitted proposals.
sentences.ja: 発表の目的と提案を出した生徒の期待を考慮し、個別点についてどれほど情報を公開すべきかも話し合う。

sentences.en: A public announcement of selected proposals might fulfill one purpose without serving as the most informative form of feedback for every group that participated.
sentences.ja: 選定提案の公表は一目的を果たしても、参加全班にとって最も有益なフィードバック形式となるとは限らない。

sentences.en: The example does not establish a legally or educationally appropriate selection procedure for any actual competition, but illustrates why the evaluation of an activity and the communication of its results require related yet distinct decisions.
sentences.ja: 例は実際の競技に法的・教育的に適切な選択手順を確立しないが、活動評価と結果伝達が関連するが別個の判断を必要とする理由を例示する。

sentences.en: A ranking does not become meaningless simply because it provides incomplete information about the objects being ranked.
sentences.ja: 順位は対象について不完全な情報を提供するだけで無意味になるわけではない。

sentences.en: Its usefulness depends on whether readers understand which characteristics were evaluated and which conclusions can reasonably be drawn from the resulting order.
sentences.ja: 有用性はどの特性が評価され、結果順からどの結論を合理的に導けるか読者が理解するかに依存する。

sentences.en: Responsible evaluation consequently involves considering how the information provided may affect the people whose work has been evaluated.
sentences.ja: 責任ある評価には提供情報が評価対象の人々にどう影響し得るか考慮することが伴う。

sentences.en: The promise of a ranking should be no greater than the questions that the underlying evaluation can legitimately help answer.
sentences.ja: 順位の約束は根底の評価が正当に答えられる問いを超えるべきではない。

questions.prompt: Why might rankings be ethically significant?
options: They always contain complete accounts of every participant.
They may affect opportunities despite summarizing only selected characteristics.
They never influence a decision.
They are impossible to communicate publicly.
questions.explanation_ja: 限られた評価でも機会に影響。

questions.prompt: Why must the organizers select among proposals?
options: All groups have submitted identical plans.
The community has no need for activities.
The organizers cannot read the proposals.
Available resources can support only a limited number.
Group size, age and personal popularity.
Only the number of words.
Contribution, feasibility and explanation of plans.
Only the amount of money requested.
questions.explanation_ja: 貢献・実現可能性・説明。

questions.prompt: What concern does the second organizer raise?
options: A rank may not give groups useful information for improvement.
Publishing results necessarily makes selection impossible.
Every group should receive identical support.
The criteria cannot be used in evaluation.

questions.prompt: What do the two hypothetical proposals illustrate?
options: All proposals with similar scores must have identical quality.
Feasibility alone measures every aspect.
Numerical evaluation never permits comparison.
Similar combined scores can conceal different strengths and weaknesses.

questions.prompt: What does a small score difference not establish?
options: A difference in the combined scores.
Superiority in every respect.
An order based on the selected measure.
The existence of different criteria.
questions.explanation_ja: 全側面で優位であるとは言えない。

questions.prompt: What kind of feedback is considered?
options: Information linking the criteria to features of each proposal.
A single unexplained rank for every group.
An announcement of unrelated projects.
Only the names of the judges.

questions.prompt: Why distinguish a public announcement from individual feedback?
options: Both necessarily require identical information.
Every score must be disclosed publicly in all circumstances.
They can serve different informational purposes.
Individual explanations prevent any selection.
In an accidental manner.
In a justified or valid manner.
In a completely secret way.
In a numerically precise manner only.

questions.prompt: Which statement best expresses the argument?
options: Rankings can be useful if interpreted within their evaluative scope and communicated with attention to affected people.
Rankings should be treated as complete measures of everyone's worth.
A difference in score establishes superiority in every characteristic.
The purpose of feedback is always identical to that of public selection.
questions.explanation_ja: 評価範囲と伝達の影響。
